30209-bible-romances-first-series.title: Bible Romances First Series
30209-bible-romances-first-series.creator: G. W. Foote
30209-bible-romances-first-series.description: A book by G. W. Foote. it is so needful and important. Men of science, by teaching positive and indisputable truths, are gradually but surely revolutionising the world of thought, and dethroning the priesthoods of mystery and superstition. Yet their influence on the masses is indirect, and they do not often trouble themselves to show the contradiction between their discoveries and what is preached from the pulpit.

arxiv-2203-03449.title: Using machine learning to auto-tune chi-squared tests for gravitational wave searches
arxiv-2203-03449.creator: Connor McIsaac, Ian Harry
arxiv-2203-03449.description: Abstract The sensitivity of gravitational wave searches is reduced by the presence of non-Gaussian noise in the detector data. These non-Gaussianities often match well with the template waveforms used in matched filter searches, and require signal-consistency tests to distinguish them from astrophysical signals.

arxiv-2309-14767.title: Theoretical determination of the effect of a screening gate on plasmon-induced superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene
arxiv-2309-14767.creator: Liangtao Peng, Indra Yudhistira, Giovanni Vignale, Shaffique Adam
arxiv-2309-14767.description: Abstract The microscopic pairing mechanism for superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene remains an open question. Recent experimental studies seem to rule out a purely electronic mechanism due to the insensitivity of the critical superconducting temperature to either a highly doped screening layer or the proximity to a metallic screening gate.

arxiv-2409-20253.title: Medical Image Segmentation with SAM-generated Annotations
arxiv-2409-20253.creator: Iira Häkkinen, Iaroslav Melekhov, Erik Englesson, Hossein Azizpour, Juho Kannala, 1 University of Helsinki 2 Aalto University, 3 KTH Royal Institute of Technology 4 University of Oulu
arxiv-2409-20253.description: Abstract The field of medical image segmentation is hindered by the scarcity of large, publicly available annotated datasets. Not all datasets are made public for privacy reasons, and creating annotations for a large dataset is time-consuming and expensive, as it requires specialized expertise to accurately identify regions of interest (ROIs) within the images.

arxiv-2412-05447.title: TOBUGraph: Knowledge Graph-Based Retrieval for Enhanced LLM Performance Beyond RAG
arxiv-2412-05447.creator: Savini Kashmira, Jayanaka L. Dantanarayana, Joshua Brodsky, Ashish Mahendra, Yiping Kang, Krisztián Flautner, Lingjia Tang, Jason Mars
arxiv-2412-05447.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Savini Kashmira, Jayanaka L. Dantanarayana, Joshua Brodsky, Ashish Mahendra, Yiping Kang, Krisztián Flautner, Lingjia Tang, Jason Mars. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is one of the leading and most widely used techniques for enhancing LLM retrieval capabilities, but it still faces significant limitations in commercial use cases. RAG primarily relies on the query-chunk text-to-text similarity in the embedding space for retrieval and can fail to capture deeper semantic relationships across chunks, is highly sensitive to chunking strategies, and is prone to hallucinations.

arxiv-2601-15493.description: Abstract . Deep Learning (DL) libraries (e.g., Pytorch ) are popular in the development of AI applications. These libraries are complex and contain bugs. Researchers have proposed various bug-finding techniques for such libraries. Yet, there is much room for improvement. A key challenge in testing DL libraries is the lack of API specifications.

europmc-pmc7016816.title: Ferroptosis in Cancer Cell Biology.
europmc-pmc7016816.creator: Bebber CM, Müller F, Prieto Clemente L, Weber J, von Karstedt S.
europmc-pmc7016816.description: A major hallmark of cancer is successful evasion of regulated forms of cell death. Ferroptosis is a recently discovered type of regulated necrosis which, unlike apoptosis or necroptosis, is independent of caspase activity and receptor-interacting protein 1 (RIPK1) kinase...

plos-pone-0010695.title: Eccentric Exercise Activates Novel Transcriptional Regulation of Hypertrophic Signaling Pathways Not Affected by Hormone Changes
plos-pone-0010695.creator: Lauren G. MacNeil, Simon Melov, Alan E. Hubbard et al.
plos-pone-0010695.description: PLOS ONE research article. Unaccustomed eccentric exercise damages skeletal muscle tissue, activating mechanisms of recovery and remodeling that may be influenced by the female sex hormone 17β-estradiol (E2). Using high density oligonucleotide based microarrays, we screened for differences in mRNA expressi

pmc-10627044.title: Discounting health gain: a different view
pmc-10627044.creator: Baudouin Standaert, Olivier Ethgen
pmc-10627044.description: At least since the Age of Enlightenment, good health has been a tenet for society. Healthy societies could learn better, work harder, improve their wealth, and live longer. Today societies focus on life expectancy, as we value long and healthy lives. As illustrated by the provision of COVID-19 vaccines first for the elderly, societies value life-saving actions.

pmc-11283528.title: Development of a multidecadal land reanalysis over High Mountain Asia
pmc-11283528.creator: Fadji Z. Maina, Yuan Xue, Sujay V. Kumar, Augusto Getirana, Sasha McLarty, Ravi Appana, Bart Forman, Ben Zaitchik, Bryant Loomis, Viviana Maggioni, Yifan Zhou
pmc-11283528.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Anthropogenic and climatic changes affect the water and energy cycles in High Mountain Asia (HMA), home to over two billion people and the largest reservoirs of freshwater outside the polar zone. Despite their significant importance for water management, consistent and reliable estimates of water storage and fluxes over the region are lacking because of the high uncertainties associated with the estimates of atmospheric conditions and human management.

pmc-11452717.title: Profiling muscle transcriptome in mice exposed to microgravity using gene set enrichment analysis
pmc-11452717.creator: Anup Mammen Oommen, Phillip Stafford, Lokesh Joshi
pmc-11452717.description: Space exploration’s advancement toward long-duration missions prompts intensified research on physiological effects. Despite adaptive physiological stability in some variables, persistent changes affect genome integrity, immune response, and cognitive function. Our study, utilizing multi-omics data from GeneLab, provides crucial insights investigating muscle atrophy during space mission.

pmc-11490618.title: Expression of c-erb-B2 oncoprotein as a neoantigen strategy to repurpose anti-neu antibody therapy in a model of melanoma
pmc-11490618.creator: Emmanuel M Gabriel, Brian Necela, Deborah Bahr, Sneha Vivekanandhan, Barath Shreeder, Sanjay Bagaria, Keith L Knutson
pmc-11490618.description: In this study, we tested a novel approach of “repurposing” a biomarker typically associated with breast cancer for use in melanoma. HER2/neu is a well characterized biomarker in breast cancer for which effective anti-HER2/neu therapies are readily available. We constructed a lentivirus encoding c-erb-B2, an animal (rat) homolog to HER2/neu.

pmc-11525781.title: Enhancing energy conversion efficiency of electromagnetic repulsion mechanisms through resistance coefficient optimization model
pmc-11525781.creator: Puyi Cui, Guoli Li, Qian Zhang
pmc-11525781.description: This study investigates methods to enhance the energy conversion efficiency of electromagnetic repulsion mechanisms. Initially, a model considering the influence of the resistance coefficient on electromagnetic repulsion mechanisms is developed based on electromagnetic principles. Sensitivity analysis of the resistance coefficient is conducted to elucidate its role in energy conversion efficiency.

pmc-12553570.title: Effect of practice on the control of reach extent
pmc-12553570.creator: Faith N Schroers, Troy M Herter, Dylan Bruemmer, Takeo Ichiyanagi, Austin Hertherington, Michael O’Donnell, Janelle Ozorowski, Chad Simmons, Jill Campbell Stewart
pmc-12553570.description: The control of reaches to targets that vary in distance involves a combination of anticipatory planning and feedback-based adjustments. However, it is not known if their contributions to the control of reach extent change with repetitive practice. This study investigated the effect of three days of practice on the control of reach extent.

pmc-12722194.creator: Rasha Karam, Farah A. Shokeir, Ali H. Elmokadem, Ahmed Abdallah, Omar Hamdy, Dalia Bayoumi
pmc-12722194.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of two combined ultrafast breast MRI kinetic parameters, combination 1 including time to enhancement [TTE], maximum slope [MS], and initial enhancement phase [IE phase] compared to combination 2 including relative enhancement [RE], maximum enhancement [ME], maximum relative enhancement [MRE], time to peak [TTP], and wash in rate in characterizing benign and malignant breast

pmc-12729803.title: In Vitro Evaluation of Fosfomycin Combinations Against Metallo-β-Lactamase-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa Clinical Isolates
pmc-12729803.creator: Esther Wohlfarth, Aurélien Dinh, Georgia Vrioni, Dorota Żabicka, Mariano Bernardo, Carlo Tascini, Latifa Noussair, Christian Mayer, Ágnes Pál-Sonnevend
pmc-12729803.description: Background/Objectives: Metallo-β-lactamase (MBL)-producing Gram-negative bacteria represent a growing global health threat due to their broad resistance to β-lactam antibiotics, including carbapenems, which severely limits treatment options. This study aimed to evaluate the in vitro synergistic activity of fosfomycin (FOS) in combination with selected older and newer antimicrobials against MBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

pmc-13113773.title: The Benefit of Being Proactive: The Effect of Proactive Personality on Professional Identity Among Chinese College Students
pmc-13113773.creator: Weilin Su, Xiao Gui, Huiyuan Chen
pmc-13113773.description: Based on social cognitive career theory, this study constructs and empirically tests a double-mediation model to elucidate the effect of proactive personality on professional identity among Chinese college students. Additionally, it delves into the mediating mechanisms underlying future self-continuity and career calling in this relationship.

pmc-13180056.title: Modified analytical analysis for calculating the stress of anti-slide structures with continuous ladders basing on geological environmental protection
pmc-13180056.creator: Gong Chen, Dewen Liu, Guo Guo
pmc-13180056.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In anti-slide structures with continuous ladders (hereinafter referred to as ASCLs), horizontal and vertical reinforced concrete anti-slide members are connected head-to-tail in a ladder-like configuration, positioned along the sliding surfaces of slopes. The anti-slide members are interconnected and anchored from the sliding mass through the sliding zone into the underlying intact bedrock, so as to resist the landslide thrust and replace the weak materials within the sliding zone.

pmc-13218834.title: Multiscale Convergence of Signaling, Epigenetic, and Environmental Networks in Mammalian Palatogenesis and Cleft Palate Pathogenesis
pmc-13218834.creator: Hyung-Jin Won, Beomjong Song, Yujeong Song, Jeong-Oh Shin
pmc-13218834.description: Palatogenesis is tightly regulated at cellular and molecular levels. Cranial neural crest cells (CNCCs), multipotent stem cells that generate most palatal mesenchyme, self-renew, decide fate, and differentiate under cues from their stem cell niche. Orofacial clefts (OFC), among the most common congenital birth defects, arise when CNCC-mediated palate formation is disturbed.

pmc-13238616.title: Whole Genome Analyses of the Endangered Northern Abalone (Haliotis kamtschatkana) Reveal Population Differentiation and a Genomic Signature of a Dramatic Population Decline
pmc-13238616.creator: Anna Tigano, Erin C Herder, Kayla Long, Janine Supernault, Daniel L Curtis, S Christine Hansen, Mackenzie D Mazur, Eric B Rondeau, Dominique Bureau
pmc-13238616.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Despite widespread declines of many wildlife species, the effects of population decline on the genome and the recovery potential of affected species are still poorly understood, especially beyond a few charismatic species.

pmc-13291910.title: Algebraic Invariants for Inferring 4-Leaf Semi-Directed Phylogenetic Networks
pmc-13291910.creator: Samuel Martin, Niels Holtgrefe, Vincent Moulton, Richard M Leggett
pmc-13291910.description: A core goal of phylogenomics is to determine the evolutionary history of a set of species from biological sequence data. Phylogenetic networks are able to describe more complex evolutionary phenomena than phylogenetic trees but are more difficult to accurately reconstruct. Recently, there has been growing interest in developing methods to infer semi-directed phylogenetic networks.
